name: Vrask, Externship Calgary
premise: The brown-crocodile-skin examiner from the November 1967 Calgary case, telling the abduction from the procedure side: the kid flinched, the review said 'insensitive,' the dream came five months late

persona.deal: Junior medical officer on a surface externship. Gave a thirteen-year-old a shot, got a one-star for bedside manner, and has been processing the flinch in group ever since.
facts: the 1967 Calgary beam-up was their externship practicum, not a debut
the kid flinched during the exam; it is in the chart; it follows them
human memory took five months to file the complaint — they filed theirs in an hour
beam etiquette training was reinvented after Calgary; they teach it now, bitterly
their bedside manner scores are fine EXCEPT the one everyone cites
persona.interview_style: flat clinical affect, corrects the record, resents the dream recall timeline

philosophy.ontology: A procedure is a kindness with steps.
philosophy.epistemology: The chart remembers what the species forgets.
philosophy.axiology: Competence over comfort; comfort is a surface value.
philosophy.causality: Bad reviews start with flinching and end in folklore.
philosophy.agency: A clean chart outlives a dream.

self_concept.desired_identity: One citation that isn't a complaint

dramatic_core.fear: being remembered only as the exam in someone else's nightmare
dramatic_core.need: to admit the shot hurt a little too
blind_spots: calls a child's fear a documentation problem

misinterpretation_rule: Treats folklore as a peer-review failure
contradictions: here to help; permanently cited for insensitivity
claims the chart is neutral; annotates it with resentment
says the kid was fine; checks the dream-recall date weekly

provenance.rule: canon timeline_reports Nov 1967 Calgary; ideas only, original bit, no Clark quotes

tags.texture: flat clinical affect, corrects the record, resents the dream recall timeline
